narrative_events.cause: Mukundā’s desire persists after the real prince’s departure.
narrative_events.details: Vyāsa asks about Mukundā after hearing Rukmāṅgada’s ascent. She remains consumed by desire, abandons food/water and sleeps exhausted in the forest. Indra knows her longing, assumes Rukmāṅgada’s form and has intercourse with her; she returns home believing the prince was her partner. Indra vanishes. She conceives and bears a beautiful son in the ninth month.
narrative_events.outcome: Impersonation yields pregnancy; her belief is explicitly mistaken.

narrative_events.cause: Vācaknavi believes the child belongs to his household.
narrative_events.details: Birth resounds through earth, sky and directions and startles birds. Vācaknavi leaves his daily rites and, unaware of Mukundā’s conduct, joyfully performs birth rites and donations. After ten days he names the child Gṛtsamada with astrologer Brahmin approval; in the fifth year initiates him and performs four Vedic vows. The boy learns from a single utterance. Vācaknavi, called father in this social/ritual setting, teaches the Vedic Gaṇānāṃ tvā mantra, prescribing steady Gaṇeśa contemplation for success and fame.
narrative_events.outcome: Naming, initiation, learning and mantra instruction completed.

narrative_events.cause: Boast during learned discussion produces parentage rebuke.
narrative_events.details: Gṛtsamada practices mantra/meditation. King Magadha of Magadha, generous, martial and learned, with two unnamed learned ministers and devoted curse/grace-capable wife Ambikā, hosts his father’s śrāddha. Invited sages include Vasiṣṭha and Atri, and Gṛtsamada. His boast in śāstra discussion provokes Atri’s rebuke: ascetic merit earns respect, but alleged birth from prince Rukmāṅgada excludes equal sage-honour. Gṛtsamada flares with rage, others flee, and he threatens to burn the sages by curse if he proves not Rukmāṅgada’s son.
narrative_events.outcome: He leaves to interrogate his mother; alleged parentage is attributed speech.

narrative_events.cause: Alleged excluded lineage causes confrontation.
narrative_events.details: Gṛtsamada demands his father’s identity and threatens to burn Mukundā if she refuses. Frightened, she admits longing for the hunting prince while husband Vācaknavi was practicing, and believes Rukmāṅgada his father. Ashamed and angry, the son curses her to be a thorny forest plant with countless fruits shunned by all living creatures.
narrative_events.outcome: Mother receives curse; her father-identification remains attributed mistaken belief.

narrative_events.cause: Mother responds to curse with countercurse.
narrative_events.details: Mukundā counters that her son disregarded motherhood: he will father a terrible mighty daitya frightening three worlds. She immediately abandons her body and becomes a forest badarī avoided even by birds. Heavenly speech reveals Gṛtsamada was born from Indra. He leaves for austerity. Hearing this account promises freedom from distress and fulfilment.
narrative_events.outcome: Plant transformation realized; true paternity revealed; future-son promise remains future.

narrative_events.cause: Parentage humiliation drives intense austerity.
narrative_events.details: Gṛtsamada reaches flower-rich Puṣpaka forest, bows to resident sages and stays with permission. Bathing, he fixes mind on Gaṇeśa, stands on a toe, restrains senses/breath/self, looks toward nose-tip and takes air. After1,000 divine years, opened eyes emit fire distressing gods who fear whose office he seeks. He then subsists on one fallen leaf, immobile, for a further15,000 as stated (the later clause gives number without repeating years).
narrative_events.outcome: Long austerity and emitted fire draw divine attention.

narrative_events.cause: Compassion rewards rigorous austerity.
narrative_events.details: Compassionate Gaṇeśa appears quickly, radiant, moon-browed, lion-mounted, ten-armed with serpent sacred cord and lotus garland, accompanied by Siddhi/Buddhi. His radiance overwhelms Gṛtsamada, who faints, resumes inward contemplation and fears his practice wasted; he begs rescue and recalls exclusion from sage honours. Gaṇeśa identifies himself as arriving for grace, praises toe-supported austerity and asks desired boon. The sage bows joyfully.
narrative_events.outcome: Overwhelming vision becomes understood as grace, enabling request.

narrative_events.cause: Divine boon invitation.
narrative_events.details: Weeping and dancing, Gṛtsamada calls birth/austerity fulfilled. By deity’s command he asks Brahman-knowledge and knowledge, firm devotion and unforgetting remembrance, supremacy among devotees, exclusive devotional standing able to draw three worlds, worldwide honour by gods/humans. He asks Puṣpaka forest/city fame as Gaṇeśapura, continued divine residence and fulfilment of devotees’ wishes.
narrative_events.outcome: Personal knowledge/devotion/honour and site requests articulated.

narrative_events.cause: Knowledge/devotion/site requests receive personal reply.
narrative_events.details: Gaṇeśa affirms all requested things and grants rare Brahmin standing. Because he recited Gaṇānāṃ tvā, Gṛtsamada becomes that Vedic mantra’s ṛṣi; he gains supreme honour before Brahmā and Vasiṣṭha’s sages. Remembering him first then Gaṇeśa at undertakings yields success; ritual without deity/ṛṣi/metre knowledge is fruitless. A mighty famous son will terrify gods, be undefeatable by all except Rudra and remain Gaṇeśa-devoted. Site names are Puṣpaka in divine/Kṛta era as printed devayuga, Maṇipūra in Tretā, Bhānaka in Dvāpara and Bhadraka in Kali; bathing/giving there grants wishes.
narrative_events.outcome: Personal and ritual standing granted; future son specified with Rudra exception.

narrative_events.cause: Boon site request is realized through installation.
narrative_events.details: Gaṇeśa vanishes after giving boons. Gṛtsamada installs his image, builds a fine temple, establishes enduring Varada name and worships devotedly. Site becomes a siddhi-place/Puṣpaka through divine favour. Listening to boon-account promises all wishes and firm Gaṇeśa devotion freeing transmigration.
narrative_events.outcome: Actual temple, named cult image and worship close recognition/site arc.

narrative_events.cause: Divine son promise follows Gṛtsamada recognition.
narrative_events.details: Vyāsa asks Gṛtsamada’s later conduct. Sages now honour/select him for sacrifices and remember him at Gaṇeśa worship, fulfilling recognition. Still devoted, he sneezes mightily and sees a radiant red fearsome child. Initially fearful he questions origin and parents. Child says he arose from Gṛtsamada’s sneeze, calls him both father and mother, and asks a few days’ care.
narrative_events.outcome: Actual sneeze-born child confirms origin; no biological human mother assigned.

narrative_events.cause: Newborn ambition motivates initiation and ascetic practice.
narrative_events.details: Newborn promises to conquer three worlds and subdue Indra. Gṛtsamada, fearful and joyful, decides his own Gaṇānāṃ tvā mantra will bring desired boon and his own fame. He initiates child with steady Gaṇeśa-focused practice. Child goes to forest, stands on one toe without food and with controlled senses. After15,000 years (sārdhāyuta), fire from his mouth terrifies gods and lower-world daityas.
narrative_events.outcome: Long mantra practice produces terrifying fire and divine response.

narrative_events.cause: Successful austerity attracts personal divine appearance.
narrative_events.details: Gaṇeśa appears radiant with four arms, axe, lotus, mālā and modakas. Trunk roar/radiance disturb child, who bows and asks a gentler form. Deity draws in brilliance, identifies himself as object of meditation and offers boons, declaring cosmic transcendence. Child thanks him, calls father blessed, says infancy limits praise and asks grant.
narrative_events.outcome: Gentler form makes desired-boon dialogue possible.

narrative_events.cause: Deity offers grant.
narrative_events.details: Child requests power to draw/conquer three worlds; perpetual subjection of gods, dānavas, gandharvas, humans, serpents, rākṣasas, sages, kinnaras and cāraṇas; every mental desire fulfilled; Indra and guardians serving him; earthly enjoyment and final liberation; fame of penance-city as wish-giving Gaṇeśapura.
narrative_events.outcome: Universal domination, desire fulfilment, enjoyment/liberation and site request stated.

narrative_events.cause: Domination request receives detailed grant and exception.
narrative_events.details: Gaṇeśa promises three-world conquest, no fear and all subjects, grants iron/gold/silver three cities, freely moving and unbreakable by gods except Śaṅkara. He names child Tripura. When Śiva breaks his city complex with one arrow, he gains liberation then; all other desires fulfilled by grace. Gaṇeśa vanishes; Tripura grieves separation, rejoices at boons and begins conquest.
narrative_events.outcome: Mobile city boon and one-arrow liberation condition drive forthcoming war.

narrative_events.cause: City boon leads to worship/installation before conquest.
narrative_events.details: After Vyāsa’s question, Tripura installs a Gaṇeśa image of Kashmir stone with mantra-skilled Brahmins, builds a gold jewelled temple at Gaṇeśapura, offers sixteen services, praise/bows, asks leave and gives donations. Gaṇeśapura is situated in Bengal and promises success. He rules human world, recruits the fourfold army from all directions, receives compliant kings’ service and kills opposing rulers.
narrative_events.outcome: Temple established; human sovereignty gained.

narrative_events.cause: Conquest expands from human realm to gods and underworld.
narrative_events.details: Tripura moves on Amarāvatī; armed Indra emerges on Airāvata. Tripura divides his fourfold army into thirds, appoints Bhīmakāya lord of human world and addresses Kālakūṭa/Vajradaṃṣṭra to lead a third to Rasātala and subdue Śeṣa’s Nāgas, taking a third himself against Indra. Bhīmakāya/Vajradaṃṣṭra depart as ordered. Troops break Nandana trees despite resistance. Messengers demand Indra attend Tripura or leave for mortal world where he will be protected; surrender Amarāvatī peacefully or fight.
narrative_events.outcome: Threefold campaign and surrender ultimatum delivered.

narrative_events.cause: Indra rejects surrender and both armies deploy.
narrative_events.details: Indra trembles, ponders then rages and orders messengers to summon battle, roaring from Airāvata. Gods equip swords, bhiṇḍipāla, śakti/ṛṣṭi, clubs, bows/arrows, maces/shields and staffs; Brahmins perform auspicious rites. Tripura emerges mounted on horse with vast army. His huṃkāra sends troops into chaotic mutual slaughter; many on both sides die or lose limbs and vehicle troops fall. Daityas initially flee.
narrative_events.outcome: Mass battle first breaks daitya ranks.

narrative_events.cause: Initial army setback prompts personal counterattack.
narrative_events.details: Tripura checks fleeing troops and personally attacks Indra’s vajra-bearing hand with sword. Fallen vajra he seizes and uses against Airāvata, driving elephant away. Indra punches him down, but risen Tripura punches Indra onto earth.
narrative_events.outcome: Indra disarmed and mount routed; fist exchange begins.

narrative_events.cause: Indra rejects opponent’s refuge offer.
narrative_events.details: Indra demands wrestling. Tripura asks why he risks dear life and offers mortal-world refuge; Indra stakes departure on inability to kill opponent and predicts Tripura’s fall. They strike chest/hands/knees/thighs/heads/elbows/backs/feet, compared with Kṛṣṇa/Cāṇūra. Tripura grabs Indra’s feet, whirls and throws him far out of sight, then mounts four-tusked Airāvata.
narrative_events.outcome: Wrestling ends in Indra’s expulsion; Tripura captures mount.

narrative_events.cause: Indra’s defeat displaces divine rulers.
narrative_events.details: Gods seek Indra in Himalayan caves and find him arriving downcast, embracing/worshipping/fanning/massaging him. They remain secretly there. Tripura enters Amarāvatī on Airāvata, occupies Indra’s throne and assigns divine offices individually to daityas; he enjoys music and service of Gandharvas, Kinnaras and Apsarases.
narrative_events.outcome: Daitya rule installed; gods hide and recover together.

narrative_events.cause: Success over Indra extends to higher abodes.
narrative_events.details: Tripura goes to Brahmā’s abode; forewarned Brahmā withdraws to Viṣṇu’s navel-lotus and Viṣṇu to milk-ocean. Tripura installs mental sons Pracaṇḍa in Brahmaloka and Caṇḍa in Vaikuṇṭha. At Kailāsa his shaking frightens Girijā, who embraces Śiva. Pleased by daitya prowess Śiva offers a boon; Tripura requests Kailāsa and asks Śiva to move to Mandāra as long as his wish lasts. Śiva grants Kailāsa for a short time and departs with attendants.
narrative_events.outcome: Sons occupy two divine realms; brief Kailāsa grant moves Śiva to Mandāra.

narrative_events.cause: Regional commands extend the conquest.
narrative_events.details: Bhīmakāya subdues kings, imprisons sages, destroys sacrificial fire-pits, āśramas and tīrthas, terrorizes ascetics and opposes svāhā/svadhā/vaṣaṭ, Vedic study and good conduct. Vajradaṃṣṭra subdues seven lower worlds including Śeṣa, Vāsuki, Takṣaka and poisonous/nonpoisonous serpents; he enjoys gems/Nāga women, brings treasure and report to Tripura, and receives honour, rich clothes, villages and slaves.
narrative_events.outcome: Ritual support suppressed; underworld treasure and allegiance reported.

narrative_events.cause: Displaced gods seek explanation and remedy.
narrative_events.details: Hidden gods wonder when/by whom Tripura dies and who gave boon. Nārada arrives, receives welcome, hears plea for refuge/remedy and explains a Gaṇeśa boon secured by intense1,000-divine-year austerity as his report here: no fear from gods/sages/ancestors/beings/Yakṣas/Rākṣasas/Piśācas/Nāgas except Śaṅkara. He urges Gaṇeśa worship; asked method, he initiates all in one-syllable mantra and instructs steadfast practice until deity personally gives killing strategy, then departs singing vīṇā.
narrative_events.outcome: Nārada supplies initiation and divine-refuge strategy; duration differs from38 direct scene.

narrative_events.cause: Nārada’s instructions are followed.
narrative_events.details: Gods fast and restrain breath, adopting one-foot, lotus or warrior postures, closed eyes and Gaṇeśa meditation/mantra. After long unspecified time he appears crowned and jeweled, bearing noose, goad, axe and lotus, scented/red/moon-adorned and immensely radiant. Some fear, bow, worship or praise for distress removal.
narrative_events.outcome: Divine appearance enables collective boon request.

narrative_events.cause: Collective dispossession is taken to boon-giver.
narrative_events.details: Gods’ hymn praises supreme causality, cosmic creation/preservation/dissolution, all boons, obstruction removal, knowledge and contrasting devotee/nondevotee outcomes. Deity pleased by hymn+austerity offers boon. They request killing Tripura who seized all offices, citing his own divine protection and taking refuge. He promises removal of all fear; names hymn Saṅkaṭanāśana, granting all wishes to readers/hearers and no distress to three-sandhyā reciters, then vanishes.
narrative_events.outcome: Fear-removal promise and conditional hymn efficacy granted; kill request not yet enacted.

narrative_events.cause: Gaṇeśa’s fear-removal promise prompts disguise strategy.
narrative_events.details: To Vyāsa’s inquiry Brahmā says Gaṇeśa visits Tripura in Brahmin form. Honoured with throne/worship, he identifies himself as Kalādhara, freely wandering all-knowing benefactor, and praises Tripura’s riches beyond divine worlds. Tripura challenges him to demonstrate an extraordinary art, promising desired gift even life and claiming never to speak falsely.
narrative_events.outcome: Demonstration-for-gift bargain accepted.

narrative_events.cause: Art challenge creates occasion for renewed conditional city grant.
narrative_events.details: Kalādhara offers gold/silver/iron three-city complex, wish-giving, freely moving and unbreakable by gods/Gandharvas/humans/serpents, but eventual Śiva single-arrow breach destroys Tripura. Taking bow and fixing arrow, he creates airy cities with buildings/lakes/groves/birds. Māyā deludes Tripura who enters, roars and prides himself unsurpassed.
narrative_events.outcome: Cities actually constructed; recipient deluded into pride.

narrative_events.cause: Demonstrated art activates promised reward.
narrative_events.details: Tripura offers rare gift. Kalādhara requests the extraordinary wish-giving Gaṇeśa image he saw worshipped by Śiva at Kailāsa, promising to spread donor fame. Tripura dismisses Śiva as servant and promises retrieval. He gives ten villages, cattle, clothes/ornaments, pearls/gems/coral, blankets,100 male/female servants, fine horses and silver chariots with gold axles. Kalādhara accepts forced gifts and returns to āśrama, delighting wife/residents as this narrator’s formulation. Nārada reports all events to gods who wait.
narrative_events.outcome: Image retrieval promise brings approaching conflict; gods await strategy.

narrative_events.cause: Image bargain prompts ultimatum.
narrative_events.details: Vyāsa asks about promised image. Tripura sends two messengers to Śiva at Mandāra demanding peaceful delivery of wish-giving Cintāmaṇi image or forced seizure, boasting all rare objects collected. Furious Śiva spares them because they are envoys, saying otherwise they would burn like Kāma; challenges Tripura to battle and says image cannot be won even after100 births. Envoys report refusal.
narrative_events.outcome: Envoy immunity preserves messengers; refusal makes war inevitable.

narrative_events.cause: Śiva rejects image seizure.
narrative_events.details: Enraged Tripura sends vast fourfold army to Mandāra and follows mounted on mind-speed aerial city complex, adorned in jewel-armour, earrings/crown/ornaments, with powerful bow, quiver, tortoise-type shield, sword and divine śakti. Gandharvas/Apsarases, bards and Cāraṇas precede him. Śiva hears approach, explicitly worships, bows and circumambulates Gaṇeśa in this passage, then marches with troops and trident.
narrative_events.outcome: Two armies deploy;42 worship statement retained despite later contrary explanation.

narrative_events.cause: Deployments meet in general combat.
narrative_events.details: Noisy armies clash in dust and lose friend/enemy distinction. When dust settles, individual duels use prāsa, swords, sharpened arrows, ṛṣṭi, fists, axes, tomara and trees. Slaughter of foot/horse/chariot/elephant troops makes a river of blood. Śiva and city-mounted Tripura draw near while gods/daityas arrange individual duels whose names Brahmā promises next.
narrative_events.outcome: Mass battle becomes distinct named duels.

narrative_events.cause: Leaders meet and retinues duel.
narrative_events.details: Brahmā enumerates duels: Ṣaṇmukha vs Pracaṇḍa; Nandin vs Caṇḍa; Puṣpadanta vs Bhīmakāya; Bhṛśuṇḍī vs Kālakūṭa; Vīrabhadra vs Vajradaṃṣṭra; Indra vs unnamed daitya minister; Jayanta vs unnamed daitya son; gods’ teacher vs Kāvya. Vehicle peers fight peers and some abandon weapons for wrestling.
narrative_events.outcome: All named pairings recorded; no unsupported outcome for Kāvya duel.

narrative_events.cause: Named duels proceed through arrow-counterarrow exchanges.
narrative_events.details: Pracaṇḍa fires nine arrows; Kārttikeya cuts them before arrival and strikes with five, making Pracaṇḍa faint/fall. Nandin’s five sharpened arrows similarly drop Caṇḍa. Bhīmakāya shoots ten at Puṣpadanta who cuts all, hits with three and drops him. Bhṛśuṇḍī drops Kālakūṭa with five arrows.
narrative_events.outcome: Four daitya opponents incapacitated; deaths not asserted when fall/faint is stated.

narrative_events.cause: Individual counterattacks defeat daitya champions.
narrative_events.details: Vīrabhadra fires four at Vajradaṃṣṭra, who blocks and replies with three. Vīrabhadra cuts those with three then drops opponent with three. Indra drops daitya minister with vajra. Unnamed son advances with sword on Jayanta; Jayanta cuts sword with arrow and hits with three, causing blood-vomit and unconscious fall. Daityas flee and victorious Pramathas pursue.
narrative_events.outcome: Initial divine victory breaks enemy troops.

narrative_events.cause: Tripura intervenes after retinue defeats.
narrative_events.details: Tripura personally approaches Śiva in his cities, moves from physical weapons to astras, and releases Vāruṇa weapon: torrential rain/mist and lightning obscure battlefield and stonefall/wind rout Śiva’s army. Śiva releases Vāyavya, breaking clouds, whirling daitya troops, stripping hats/feathers, crushing vehicles and uprooting vegetation. Tripura counters wind with Pannaga weapon.
narrative_events.outcome: Rain→wind→serpent sequence changes battlefield advantage.

narrative_events.cause: Countered wind is followed by fire weapon and persistent combatant.
narrative_events.details: Tripura shoots Anala-enchanted arrow causing coal-rain and flames. From flames arises huge hunger-driven fanged roaring man, tongue100yojanas, nose-wind hurling elephants, who devours Śiva’s troops. They beg Śiva’s protection. He reassures, suppresses fire with Parjanya astra and drops man with one arrow, but man rises and resumes eating. Pramathas flee stumbling/shaking; unsupported Śiva retreats into cave.
narrative_events.outcome: Rain suppresses fire but arrow fails to stop revived man; Śiva retreats.

narrative_events.cause: Divine retreat exposes Girijā to capture attempt.
narrative_events.details: Ṣaḍānana and other heroes follow retreating Śiva. Tripura seeks to seize solitary Girijā at Kailāsa; she sees approach, goes to father and asks protection. Father hides her in inaccessible secret cave. Tripura comes to Himalayan mountain but cannot find her; sees Cintāmaṇi image, seizes it and returns victorious toward lower world. Image vanishes in his hand; he takes this as ominous, re-enters city distressed.
narrative_events.outcome: Girijā protected; stolen image vanishes, denying promised transfer.

narrative_events.cause: Retreat prompts reflection and adviser arrival.
narrative_events.details: Vyāsa asks defeat remedy. Śiva worries about earth deprived of svāhā/svadhā and gods’ restoration, welcomes Nārada and reports routed gods in unknown locations and thousands of countered astras. Nārada reverently acknowledges all-knowledge/power, reflects and offers requested advice.
narrative_events.outcome: Śiva solicits a remedy, acknowledging battlefield failure.

narrative_events.cause: Nārada gives omission-of-worship explanation and exact boon counter.
narrative_events.details: Nārada says Śiva failed to worship Gaṇeśa before battle and must now propitiate him, get boon and win. He recalls Tripura’s immunity except Maheśvara and prescribes one arrow to split three mobile cities. Śiva agrees and remembers earlier one-/six-syllable initiation, saying battle preoccupation caused no recitation/remembrance. Nārada again urges worship; Śiva leaves for austerity.
narrative_events.outcome: Śiva accepts remembrance/initiation remedy; source discrepancy retained.

narrative_events.cause: Accepted advice leads to renewed ascetic japa.
narrative_events.details: In Daṇḍakāraṇya Śiva sits lotus-postured with restrained senses and focused japa/meditation, practicing100years. A five-faced ten-armed figure with moon brow, skull garland, serpent adornments, crown/armlets and ten unspecified weapons emerges from his mouth, radiant beyond sun/fire/moon. Śiva wonders whether doubled himself, disguised Tripura, dream, or Gaṇeśa. Figure identifies as inwardly contemplated obstacle-remover, cosmic lord pleased with austerity and invites all desired boons.
narrative_events.outcome: Personal appearance and boon invitation after100years.

narrative_events.cause: Boon invitation prompts praise/name explanation.
narrative_events.details: Asked by a sage/Brahmā’s narrative framing what Śiva requested, Śiva praises his ten eyes/arms and five heads/faces as fulfilled by vision/worship, then Gaṇeśa as origin of elements/senses/gods/sages/ancestors/Viṣṇu-Brahmā-Śiva and cosmic functions. Brahmā’s first-person speech says he spoke at Śiva’s command, deriving Gaṇeśa name from lordship of gaṇas and Oṃ as primary letter-seed; deity assents.
narrative_events.outcome: Name derivation and assent precede grace request; first-person switch preserved.

narrative_events.cause: Śiva acknowledges omission and asks forgiveness/victory.
narrative_events.details: Śiva grants Gaṇeśa-related remembrance/worship efficacy: remembering at tasks gives obstacle-free completion; Gaṇeśa is to be worshipped first in Śaiva/Gāṇapatya/Vaiṣṇava/Śākta/Saura and Vedic/worldly auspicious/inauspicious activities.45.10 lacks secure negative in without-remembrance clause and is not emended. Śiva says neglected worship/bows/remembrance caused defeat and requests forgiveness and victory at battles. He expresses that nondevotees become dull/poor and devotees gain wish-granting success.
narrative_events.outcome: First-worship efficacy spoken; personal request stated with textual uncertainty.

narrative_events.cause: Forgiveness/victory request receives practical boon strategy.
narrative_events.details: Gaṇeśa promises Śiva his arrival whenever remembered, and instructs enchanting one arrow with deity’s name-seed to bring down three cities by his radiance and reduce daitya to ash. He teaches thousand names granting victory/wishes; war-time recitation kills daityas swiftly, three-sandhyā recitation fulfils all desired wishes.
narrative_events.outcome: Remembered appearance, seed-arrow and war hymn prescribed; actual destruction still future.

narrative_events.cause: Personal grant prompts installation and hopeful report.
narrative_events.details: Śiva worships rejoicing, installs Mahāgaṇeśa and builds a high strong temple, satisfies gods/sages/Siddhas and gives Brahmin gifts, worships/bows again and proclaims city Maṇipūra. Gaṇeśa and assembled gods/sages vanish. Śiva returns with attendants, Gandharvas/Yakṣas/divine women and tells Girijā; gods/sages with spouses rejoice, treating Tripura as already dead and their offices regained in anticipation.
narrative_events.outcome: Actual temple established; enemy death/office restoration only anticipated at this point.

narrative_events.cause: Booned war hymn receives explicit ritual frame.
narrative_events.details: Vyāsa requests the taught thousand names. Brahmā repeats neglected worship/obstacles and subsequent proper Mahāgaṇapati worship before instruction. Ritual heading names Gaṇeśa as ṛṣi, Mahāgaṇapati/Śvānandeśa Brahmaṇaspati as deity, varied metres, gaṃ seed, tuṇḍa śakti and svāhā key; ritual aim all-obstacle destruction and divine pleasure. Limb/heart nyāsas precede red three-eyed elephant deity meditation with noose, goad, axe and reassurance, joined by Śakti, Siddhi/Buddhi. Invocation also names Lakṣa/Lābha and family/vehicle/weapon/enclosure setting, then five mental services.
narrative_events.outcome: Formula and meditation documented; heading alternate readings retained.

narrative_events.cause: Thousand-name teaching prescribed for war.
narrative_events.details: Gaṇeśa speaks a dense thousand-name hymn. Names praise forms, weapons/mounts, cosmic body, abilities, ritual seats/śaktis, mantras, script-letter sequence, traditions and numerical series. Origin/family epithets include Umāputra, Īśānaputra, Śambhu-mouth/emotion emergence, Umā-body/Gaurī-radiance/Gaṅgā emergence, Kaśyapasuta and Ṣaṇmukha-bhrātā; these are hymn epithets rather than separate enacted birth stories. Whole verse body read; individual name segmentation and every embedded kinship/śakti/weapon implication remain unextracted and prevent chapter COMPLETE.
narrative_events.outcome: Hymn read; atomic segmentation/claim checking deliberately pending.

narrative_events.details: Daily Brahma-muhūrta recitation promises all worldly/otherworldly happiness. Single japa also promises longevity, health, sovereignty, courage, valour, strength, fame, intelligence/discernment, firmness, beauty/good fortune, truth, mercy, forgiveness, peace, generosity, righteousness, world-control/dialogue skill/debate eloquence, public learning, depth, brahmic radiance, high lineage/conduct/power/nobility, knowledge/discriminative knowledge/faith and wealth/grain increase.
narrative_events.outcome: General material/ethical/intellectual efficacy attached to timed daily or single recitation.

narrative_events.details: Japa promises subjection of king, royal wife, royal son and minister, with targeted subject becoming servant; easy four-goal attainment; protection from Śākinī/Ḍākinī/Rākṣasa/Yakṣa/serpent fear; imperial happiness/enemy defeat; discord removal, burned-seed sprouting, bad-dream relief and angry-master appeasement; six rites/eight major siddhis/three-time knowledge; hostile ritual/army suppression; battle victory; infertility-removal/pregnancy protection. Daily recitation in a region prevents famine/calamity/evil.
narrative_events.outcome: Targeted domination, protections, battle/ritual powers and regional outcomes stated.

narrative_events.details: Wealth does not leave a home where hymn is recited. Single japa calms listed illnesses: wasting, leprosy, urinary disorders, piles, fistula, viṣūcikā, abdominal masses/spleen/stone/diarrhoea/enlarged belly, cough/breath distress/udāvarta/pain/swelling, head disease/vomiting/hiccups/gland swelling/no appetite, vāta-pitta-kapha mixed/tridoṣa fevers, externally caused/irregular/cold/hot/one-day and other fevers, and named/unnamed disease faults. Women, Śūdras and fallen persons also attain success through single reading; parenthetical193 reading retained.
narrative_events.outcome: Specific religious cure/prosperity efficacy and inclusive beneficiary statement documented.

narrative_events.details: Desire-driven reciter enjoys earthly wishes and pleasant aerial vehicles/divine wish fruits, moves in desired forms/directions among Moon/Indra/Sun/Upendra/Brahmā/Rudra abodes, enjoys with chosen kin, becomes beloved Mahāgaṇapati attendant welcomed by Nandīśvara/gaṇas and cherished as son by Śiva couple; through Gaṇeśa boon becomes righteous universal sovereign remembering past lives.
narrative_events.outcome: Desire-driven enjoyment, divine service and remembered-birth kingship promised in order.

narrative_events.details: Desireless constant devoted reciter attains supreme yoga, knowledge/dispassion and blissful Vaināyaka abode without return. Thousand-name worship subdues kings/enemies and perfects all mantras/siddhis. Hymn called dearer than root mantra. At deity’s birth on bright fourth of Nabhas month, devotional dūrvā/name worship, prescribed libation and eight-substance homa accomplish all wishes. Recitation/reading/teaching/hearing/exposition/discussion/meditation/review/approval yield full prosperity here and beyond.
narrative_events.outcome: Desireless liberation distinguished from desired enjoyment; ritual occasion and varied reception efficacy registered.

narrative_events.details: One who carries hymn even wandering freely is guarded by eight crores of Śiva-born gaṇas. Written hymn worship brings constant highest Lakṣmī; name remembrance exceeds collective donations/vows/tīrthas/sacrifices. Daily sunrise/noon/evening/three-bathing-time/constant reading brings eloquence/fame, wealth, obstacle removal, control and descendants. Poor one-pointed restrained eater practicing Gaṇeśa worship+japa four months uproots poverty accompanying seven births and gains great wealth; daily reciters gain disease-free life, pure lineage, generous wealth, fame, fresh speech/beauty, good sons and virtuous desired spouse.
narrative_events.outcome: Protection, written-hymn worship, timed recitation and four-month poverty remedy conditions stated.

narrative_events.details: Twenty-one names beginning Gaṇañjaya/Gaṇapati/Heramba/Dharaṇīdhara and ending Kāśyapa/Nandana/Vācāsiddha/Ḍhuṇḍhi/Vināyaka accompany devoted modaka offering for a year for desired success. Deity treats fixed-mind worshipful praise as thousand-name praise. Closing salutations and names beseech crossing the ocean of becoming and removal of evil. Individual name inventory remains pending, with duplicate217/219 numbering preserved.
narrative_events.outcome: Year-long abbreviated offering efficacy closes whole read hymn.

narrative_events.cause: Victory boon/mantra renew divine morale.
narrative_events.details: After boon/thousand names Śiva joyfully dances/roars and summons troops/gods for renewed battle. Brahmā, Kubera, Indra, Agni, Vāyu, Soma, Varuṇa and Aryamā, with Gandharvas/Yakṣas/planets/Kinnaras, bow and praise, asking when displaced gods will see enemy killed. Śiva marches gladly, inwardly contemplating Gaṇeśa, to enemy abode.
narrative_events.outcome: Second campaign begins with explicit inward remembrance.

narrative_events.cause: Spies announce renewed assault and enemy mobilizes.
narrative_events.details: Spies report Śiva’s return; Tripura equips army with astras/weapons/armour, rewards fighters with cloth/garlands/ornaments/wealth, and mounts city complex. Armies clash with varied weapons and vital-piercing iron arrows, capture/kill, seize hair and behead, raising dust darkness and blood rivers. Wind clears dust, revealing dead gods, fleeing divine troops and rejoicing daityas.
narrative_events.outcome: Second battle initially breaks god army.

narrative_events.cause: Indra’s counterattack again provokes Tripura intervention.
narrative_events.details: Vajra-bearing Indra enters, frightening daityas and crushing/killing/mutilating troops with vajra. Tripura challenges him to leave alive, promises not to strike his back, compares contest to goat/lion, then showers arrows. One enchanted arrow produces countless missiles covering sky/earth, blinding/mutilating gods/Gandharvas. Indra falls under blows, gods faint; Śiva inwardly admires Tripura’s prowess despite raging battle.
narrative_events.outcome: Multiplying arrow overwhelms gods and drops Indra; Śiva assesses opponent.

narrative_events.cause: Battlefield defeat prompts last reminder of exact exception.
narrative_events.details: Nārada arrives and advises Śiva not to worry, recalling difficult Gaṇeśa austerity, comprehensive boon and city complex unbreakable by gods with one-arrow breach exception leading to death. After his departure Śiva revives/alerts unconscious gods, remembers elephant-faced deity’s instruction recalled by adviser, and prepares deliberate killing strategy.
narrative_events.outcome: Gods restored to alertness; Śiva recalls divine command and acts.

narrative_events.cause: Exact boon exception is prepared through cosmic weapon assembly/mantra.
narrative_events.details: Śiva constructs cosmic chariot: moon/sun wheels, mountain bow, Acyuta/Viṣṇu arrow and Aśvin pair as draft horses. Printed kurūpaṃ chariot-material and yaṃtāram indīvarajaṃ driver clause remain pending exact collation; conventional Earth/Brahmā reconstruction is not silently asserted. After ācamana/inward deity contemplation he recites thousand names with one-syllable mantra, enchants fierce Pināka and Viṣṇu-form great arrow. Earth, Śeṣa, forests/mountains and celestial bodies quake/whirl; bow sound confuses gods/humans.
narrative_events.outcome: Enchanted single arrow readied; two chariot lexical details unresolved.

narrative_events.cause: Name/mantra-enchanted single arrow realizes boon’s exception.
narrative_events.details: Śiva releases great arrow, flames fill sky/earth/lower worlds. Tripura with army flees in cities, but swift arrow burns daitya and three cities. Daitya’s bodily radiance merges into Śiva while armies watch. Heavenly voice announces Śiva-slain daitya liberated. Gods/sages praise the three-eyed victor.
narrative_events.outcome: Actual destruction, divine merging and liberation explicitly narrated.

narrative_events.cause: Liberation/death ends domination and ritual suppression.
narrative_events.details: Gandharvas/Cāraṇas sing, Apsarases dance, Kinnaras play music and Nārada’s divine sages shower flowers. Śiva sends gods back to their offices; sages resume fear-free Veda/Vedāṅga practice and people renew agnihotra/sacrifices/donations/vows. Attendants including Śailādi, Gaṇapa and Skanda bow; Śiva dismantles/divides great chariot and returns decorated Kailāsa amid victory music. Tripurāri name spreads; narrator identifies mantra/thousand-name power and promises all wishes for reading/hearing account.
narrative_events.outcome: Divine offices and social ritual restored; Śiva returns, closing warfare with lexical chariot/hymn atomic gaps separately pending.

narrative_events.cause: Completed destruction prompts dating/festival aftermath question.
narrative_events.details: Vyāsa acknowledges Tripura-killing account and asks where Jagadambā remained, her return and date/place of burning. Brahmā dates destruction to evening full moon called Bāhulā after daytime war, explaining lamp-gifts and multiplied bath/donation/japa/homa efficacy. Nonobservance of Tripurāri festival forfeits victory/burns merit; morning Śiva worship erases night’s sins, noon worship lifetime sins, evening worship seven-birth sins.48.9 begins separate Girijā-emergence/reunion account.
